Subject: Tuesday reading club — update before the review on 18 November

Dear Niamh,

I wanted to write before the review meeting on Wednesday 18 November, as there’s been a lovely change in the Tuesday reading club’s numbers since the early weeks. I also need to tell you about a conversation I had with a local reporter, which I should have checked with you about first.

Your email of 30 October said the club would be paused from January because of low attendance and the increase in the hall insurance. I understand those are real concerns, but I hope the latest figures might give us a reason to reconsider the pause.

We had five children most weeks in September, rising to nine by mid-October, and last Tuesday, 3 November, we had fourteen. I’m absolutely delighted. Since we started in September 2025, we’ve been working to build up the Tuesday sessions, from 3.30 to 4.45 in the upstairs meeting room at Knocknacarra library, and it feels as though they’re beginning to take hold.

There have been small moments that mean as much to me as the numbers. Two sisters from a Ukrainian family joined us in October, and the older girl now reads to her younger sister in English at the end of each session. Another child, who wouldn’t open a book in September, asked last week if he could take two home. After all my years teaching, that sort of thing still makes my day.

We’ve also had a very generous donation from Declan Moran at Salthill Book Nook: 120 books, mostly for the six-to-nine age group, with a good few as Gaeilge. It gives us much more choice for the children.

I know increased attendance doesn’t settle the insurance question, and one busy Tuesday isn’t the whole picture. Still, the numbers have been moving steadily in the right direction. It would be a terrible pity to stop just as the club is taking off. Would you bring these figures to the review and reconsider the January pause?

Now, about the reporter. I met Orla Keane from the Corrib Courier at the farmers’ market and got carried away telling her about the club. I said, “Come along any Tuesday.” She would now like to visit on Tuesday 24 November with a photographer.

I was wrong not to check with you first, plain and simple, and I wanted you to hear it from me. I know that photographs of the children require your sign-off and the parental consent forms. My invitation should not have got ahead of that process.

I’m happy to ring Orla and put the visit on hold until you’ve decided whether it should go ahead. If you do approve it, I can collect the consent forms myself, following your guidance. The coverage could be wonderful for the club, but only if it’s done properly.

Thank you for considering all of this, Niamh, and for your support with the volunteers. I’m very encouraged by what’s happening on Tuesdays, and I wanted you to have the fuller picture before the meeting.

Warm wishes,
[Your name]
